insights.claim: odh-observability uses the ubi9/ubi-minimal-pqc (post-quantum crypto) base image with GOEXPERIMENT=strictfipsruntime, positioning it among the earliest RHOAI components to adopt PQC-ready packaging.
insights.reasoning: The Dockerfile.konflux builds with strictfipsruntime tags and uses ubi-minimal-pqc rather than the standard ubi-minimal base. This signals an intentional migration to post-quantum crypto readiness at the container base layer, which may set a precedent for other RHOAI operator components.

insights.claim: TLS configuration for all proxy components is dynamically derived from the cluster APIServer TLSSecurityProfile rather than hardcoded, ensuring consistent cipher suite enforcement across the observability stack.
insights.reasoning: The FromAPIServer function reads the cluster APIServer object and resolves the TLS profile to concrete min version and cipher suite strings that are injected into kube-rbac-proxy arguments via Go templates. This means changing the cluster TLS profile automatically updates all observability proxy components on the next reconciliation cycle, without operator version changes.

insights.claim: The Monitoring CRD schema is structurally coupled to odh-platform-utilities via embedded PlatformObject interface, ManagementSpec, Status, and ComponentReleaseStatus types, creating a compile-time dependency on the platform API contract.
insights.reasoning: The odh-platform-utilities dependency serves two purposes: CRD type embedding (api/common) and deployment mechanics (pkg/deploy). The CRD-level coupling means breaking changes to PlatformObject, ManagementSpec, or Status in odh-platform-utilities require coordinated updates to this operator's API types. The deployment-level coupling is more loosely held via the deployer interface. This dual dependency is a deliberate platform consistency trade-off.
